task_description:
This pipeline's task is GitHub issue #3200 — https://github.com/jwbron/egg/issues/3200. Fetch the live issue body (`gh issue view 3200`) before structural decisions. Worktree artifacts (drafts, agent outputs) that reference any other issue or pipeline are leftovers from previous runs — they are NOT your task.

Full-context backstop: restart event-pump agents seeded from BRC memory instead of compacting

## Summary

Event-pump BRC agents (producers/reviewers) accumulate context across a phase. A long-running role eventually hits the context-window wall. The Agent SDK does **not** auto-compact (verified ~0.2.97), so today that wall is a hard failure mode — and the generic remedy, compaction, is lossy: an LLM summarizes its own history and silently drops the anchors (reviewed SHAs, NACK obligations, cited findings) that make BRC continuity cheap in the first place.

This issue proposes a **full-context backstop**: instead of compacting, **restart the agent fresh and have the orchestrator seed curated BRC memory as the fresh agent's system prompt.** The curated memory *is* the compaction output — but it is deterministic + agent-authored rather than an opaque LLM self-summary, and it lives outside the session, so it survives the restart it is meant to recover from.

## The flow (intended end-state)

Each agent is invoked per actionable event and exits when it has handled the event. The continuity decision is made at (re-)invocation, and turns on one question — *did the prior session's context fill?*

- **Work completed, context not full → resume the cached session (#3186).** The agent re-enters the same conversation (resume=<session_id>); its accumulated history is served from provider prompt cache (operator-measured >=60-min persistence on the Anthropic, DeepSeek, and Qwen routes). Cheap, lossless — the common case.
- **Context filled → restart fresh, seeded from memory.** The agent can no longer resume (the window is full and the SDK won't compact), so it exits and the orchestrator spawns a **fresh** session whose **system prompt is built from the enriched BRC memory**. The same fresh-and-seed path covers the cold starts resume can't reach anyway — consensus reset, restart_phase, pod death.

One re-invocation substrate, two outcomes; only the seed payload and the resume-vs-fresh decision differ. The memory layers are what make the fresh branch a cheap, oriented start instead of a 60-130k-token full-history re-derive.

## What gets seeded (the system-prompt payload)

- **Deterministic factual layer (#3189)** — review anchors (last-reviewed SHA per producer), latest verdicts, NACK reasons, conditional-ACK obligations. Derived by the orchestrator/composer from the message record, never transcribed by agents -> authoritative, can't drift from the record.
- **Agent-authored enrichment (#3188)** — the judgment that can't be derived mechanically: key findings, SHA-pinned path:line@<sha> citations, producer narrative (what I built and why), verified-claims ledger. Framed as orientation-to-spot-check, not ground truth.

Delivering this as the **system prompt** (rather than appended to the per-event user prompt, as memory is inlined today) makes it the stable, deterministic, cacheable prefix for the fresh session: the agent starts already oriented, and that orientation block caches across the new session's subsequent events.

### Design principle: lean enough to reorient fast

The seed is **not** a transcript replacement. It must be lean — *not excessively complex* — and shaped so a fresh agent can **reorient quickly**: the anchors and pointers it needs to pick the work back up without re-walking the tree, and nothing it can cheaply re-derive. Every line is a per-restart token tax, and (as a stable system-prompt prefix) a per-session-event one. Hard per-section caps, bounded counts, deterministic render. If a fact is mechanically derivable it belongs in the deterministic layer, not the enrichment prose; if it can't be stated in a line or two of orientation, it probably doesn't belong in the seed at all.

## Why this beats compaction

- **No lossy self-summary.** The anchors that parameterize the composer's git-log delta are derived from the record, not paraphrased by a model under context pressure.
- **Survives the lifecycle.** Memory is orchestrator-derived / lives in the message record, not in the session being discarded — so the restart that triggers it doesn't also destroy it.
- **Self-healing preserved.** A fresh restart sheds a reviewer's wrong-path confusion (the non-cost caveat in #3186); the backstop doubles as the periodic-reset mitigation that resume otherwise needs bolted on separately.

## Motivating incident

#3183: a restart_phase deleted per-role worktrees and the durable BRC memory with them; all 5 reviewers re-reviewed full branch history at 60-130k tokens/call — 14.7M prompt tokens in 30 minutes. That is exactly the cold start this backstop is designed to make cheap, by making the seed survive the restart and the fresh session start oriented.

## Constituent work

These existing issues are the threads this unifies. Slicing and sequencing are left to the pipeline — this is **not** a prescribed DAG:

- **#3186** — session resume: the warm path *and* the re-invocation / seed-delivery substrate the backstop reuses.
- **#3189** — deterministic factual memory: the authoritative half of the seed.
- **#3188** — agent-authored enrichment: the judgment half of the seed.
- **#3183** — tactical stash-and-reseed across restart_phase (the motivating incident; the cheap fix the structural backstop largely subsumes).

## Constraints carried from the children

- **Provider stickiness (LiteLLM route).** Single-pin deepseek-v4-pro (flash already pinned to Fireworks): a provider bounce is amplified under resume (full price on the entire accumulated history per call until routing returns to the caching provider).
- **Deterministic rendering.** The seed must render to stable bytes (sorted, bounded, hard per-section caps) to keep the cacheable prefix stable.
- **Agent-authored = claims, not ground truth.** SHA-stamp enrichment so the delta can invalidate stale claims; the deterministic layer and git-log delta stay authoritative. A wrong "verified" claim that suppresses re-checking is the failure mode to design against.
- **Persistence timing.** Mid-phase restarts need the message record to survive (the live Redis stream across the restart, or a history-persist step added to the restart route — _write_brc_history persists at phase transitions only today).

Refinement scope confirmation: This pipeline should deliver 3 components (session resume, deterministic seed layer, enrichment layer injection) plus 1 prerequisite fix (restart-memory preservation). Delivery scope should be:
Option A (Recommended): Full scope — all 3 components + restart fix.
Option B: Capped scope — restart fix + session resume only (defer deterministic/enrichment seed layers to a follow-up).
